items.title: SK하이닉스, 대규모 자사주 매입 마무리…추가 주주환원에 '눈길'

items.snippet: 지난달 21일 서부전선 비무장지대(DMZ) 지뢰 폭발사건이 발생한 지 한 달째에 접어들고 있지만 정부는 북한에 대해 구체적인 “상응조치”를 내놓지 않고 있다. 김정은 북한 국무위원장의 여동생인 김여정 노동당 총무부장이 지뢰 폭발이 자작극이라며 “즉시적이고 가차없는 보복”을 가하겠다고 위협했지만 정부는 2015년 목함지뢰 사건 당시 2주 만에 보냈던 유엔 안전보장이사회 서한조차 대응 여부를 결정하지 못하고 있는 것. 외교부는 20일 “국제사회를 대상으로 폭발의 원인이 인위적으로 매설된 북한군 지뢰로 최종 판명되었고 이는 명백한 정전협정 위반인 점을 설명하고 있다”면서도 “유엔 관련 (조치 등) 추가 조치에 대해 관계부처와 대응방안을 계속 검토할 것으로 생각한다”고 밝혔다. 앞서 우리 군은 북한 지뢰로 최종 판명되면 상응하는 조치를 하겠다고 밝혔...

items.title: 메가특구 주52시간 “예외” “불가” 법안 동시에 낸 與
items.snippet: 여당이 전남광주 반도체 클러스터 등 메가특구를 지원하기 위한 ‘초광역특구법(메가특구법)’을 발의하면서 고소득·연구직 노동자의 주 52시간제 예외 등 노동특례를 포함시킨 안과 제외한 안을 동시에 발의하기로 했다. 노동특례를 놓고 갈등이 지속되자 “연내 통과”를 못 박으며 속도를 강조했던 여당이 결론을 미룬 것이다. 더불어민주당 한병도 원내대표는 20일 “주요 쟁점인 노동시간 특례 등을 둘러싸고 다양한 의견이 있음을 잘 알고 있다”며 “특례를 포함한 안과 포함하지 않은 안 두 가지 법안을 제출한다”고 밝혔다. 민주당은 두 법안을 향후 병합 심사해 최종안을 마련하고, 여러 부처와 상임위에 걸친 쟁점을 다루기 위해 여야가 참여하는 국회 특별위원회 설치도 검토하기로 했다. 한 원내대표는 “처리 시점을 못 박지 않고 충분한 숙의와 토론을 거치겠다”고 했...

items.title: 임명장 다음날 국무회의 참석한 중수청장… 野 “정치 수사화될 판”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 20일 국무회의에 참석한 김지용 중대범죄수사청장에게 “화이트칼라 범죄나 권력형 부패 범죄, 증권·금융범죄 등 중대 범죄에 대해서 네 편 내 편 가르지 말고 일체의 성역 없이 엄단함으로써 중대범죄수사청장의 존재 의의와 필요성을 증명해 주시기 바란다”고 말했다. 김 청장은 이날 취임 후 처음으로 국무회의에 참석했다. 국민의힘은 독립성이 보장돼야 할 수사기관장의 국무회의 참석이 부적절하다고 지적하면서 “수사의 정치화는커녕 정치가 수사화될 판”이라고 비판했다. ● 李, 국무회의 나온 중수청장에 “성역 없는 수사” 이 대통령은 이날 오전 청와대에서 열린 국무회의에서 김 청장을 향해 “수사와 기소를 완전히 분리하고 공소청과 중수청의 소속 부처까지 달리하는 검찰개혁이 제도적으로 완비됐다”며 “중수청이 독립적인 중대 범죄 수사기관으로 새출발...

items.title: 정부, 우크라 대사 소환 이어 공관원 절반 철수
items.snippet: 정부가 20일 우크라이나에 주재하는 한국대사관 공관원 절반가량을 철수시키기로 했다. 정부가 8일 박기창 주우크라이나 대사를 소환했는데도 우크라이나가 북한군 포로의 한국 송환 비공개 합의를 깬 것을 공개 사과하지 않자 추가 조치를 취한 것이다. 박두순 외교부 대변인은 20일 정례브리핑에서 “주우크라이나 대사 소환 조치 이후에도 우크라이나 측의 전향적 조치가 없는 상황”이라며 “우크라이나 전역에 걸친 공습 위협이 상존해 안전 확보가 어려운 점 등을 고려해 공관원 일부 철수를 결정했다”고 밝혔다. 해외 공관원 철수는 2015년 주리비아 대사관과 2021년 주아프가니스탄 대사관 사례 이후 처음이다. 다만 윤지완 대사대리와 공관원 절반가량은 현지에 남아 최소한의 외교 활동과 수십 명의 현지 교민 대피 지원 등 영사 활동을 이어갈 방침이다. 정부는 박...

items.title: 李, ‘3기 신도시’ 인천 계양지구 찾아 “신속 공급이 부동산 정책 성패 갈라”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 20일 3기 신도시 중 처음으로 올해 12월부터 입주가 시작되는 인천 계양지구를 찾아 현장을 점검하고 “3기 신도시에서의 신속한 주택 공급은 부동산 정책의 성패를 가르는 중요한 분기점이 될 것”이라며 주택 공급을 강조했다. 이 대통령은 이날 주택공급 현장 간담회를 갖고 “비상사태다”라며 “예측 가능한 공급을 통해 시장의 불안감을 해소하고 궁극적으로는 국민의 주거 안정을 이루는 데 있어서 3기 신도시가 핵심적인 역할을 해 내야겠다”며 이같이 말했다. 이어 “이미 발표한 공급 정책이 제대로 이행되지 못하는 것 같은 모습을 보이면 부동산 정책 전반에 대한 국민의 신뢰도가 떨어질 수밖에 없다”고 했다. 한국갤럽 여론조사에서 7월 4주 차부터 부동산 정책이 대통령 직무수행 부정평가 이유 1위를 기록하는 상황에서 재차 속도전을 강조한 것...

items.title: 김정은 뇌출혈설 확산… 北, 사진 공개
items.snippet: 북한 관영매체 노동신문은 김정은 북한 국무위원장(오른쪽)이 19일 딸 주애와 함께 ‘새 제품 개발과 질 제고 열풍’을 주제로 열린 ‘전국 피복, 신발 전시회’에 참석했다고 20일 보도했다. 이날 해외 온라인 커뮤니티 등에서 김 위원장이 뇌출혈로 중국 베이징의 병원으로 긴급 이송됐다는 확인되지 않은 내용이 확산한 가운데 북한 매체가 김 위원장의 행보를 공개한 것이다.

items.title: “정전협정 위반”에도 상응조치 없는새, 北 “힘에는 힘” 위협 높여
items.snippet: 정부가 서부전선 비무장지대(DMZ) 북한 지뢰 폭발사건이 ‘명백한 정전협정 위반’이라는 결론을 내리고도 뚜렷한 ‘상응조치’를 내놓지 못하고 있는 가운데 북한은 잇따라 위협 수위를 높이고 있다. 19일 접경지역 전력 증강과 대남 확성기 방송 재개까지 거론한 데 이어 20일에는 한미·미일 연합군사훈련에 “강력한 힘의 선택이 적용될 것”이라고 위협했다. 정부는 ‘단호한 대응’을 강조하고 있지만 상응 조치를 두고는 정부 내 이견으로 별다른 진척을 보이지 못하고 있다.● 軍 감시장비 추가 설치… 북한은 잇단 위협 담화 국방부는 20일 김여정 북한 노동당 총무부장이 대남확성기 방송 재개 등 적반하장식 위협을 쏟아낸 데 대해 “(북한이) 추가 도발을 감행할 경우 단호히 응징할 것”이라고 밝혔다. “북한이 (대남 확성기 방송을 재개)한다고 하면 비례적 대응...

items.title: 정부 DMZ 조사, 유엔사 거부로 2년넘게 중단
items.snippet: 정부가 2020년부터 진행해온 비무장지대(DMZ) 내부 조사가 유엔군사령부의 출입 승인 거부로 2년 5개월째 중단된 상태인 것으로 나타났다. 유엔사는 올 3월 DMZ 범위를 정하는 남방한계선(SLL)을 새로 설정했다며 통일부의 남북출입사무소 역사관 관할권에 이의를 제기해 한때 역사관 운영이 중단됐던 것으로 드러났다. 20일 통일부 등에 따르면 DMZ 내부를 조사하는 정부 조사원에 대한 유엔사의 출입 승인이 2024년 5월부터 이뤄지지 않고 있다. DMZ 내부 조사는 2018년 남북정상회담에서 합의한 ‘DMZ 평화지대화’ 후속 조치다. 2020년부터 생태계(기후에너지환경부) 산림자원(산림청) 유네스코 세계유산 잠정목록(국가유산청), 2022년부터 DMZ 내부에 있던 마을(통일부)에 대한 조사가 이뤄져 왔다. 하지만 유엔사는 윤석열 정부 시절인...

items.title: 李 “북핵은 최후 방어용” 언급 논란… “北에 잘못된 시그널 줄수도”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 북한 핵무기가 “최후 방어 무기에 해당한다”고 언급한 것을 두고 야권에서 “북한을 옹호한다”는 공세에 나서면서 논란이 커지고 있다. 북한이 전술핵을 포함한 핵탄두 및 투발 수단 다종화를 통해 핵 역량을 고도화하는 가운데 북핵 위험성을 ‘체제 방어용’으로 평가절하했다는 것. 전시작전통제권 전환 당위성을 설명하며 북핵이 전작권 전환 변수가 되기 어렵다는 취지이지만 자칫 북한에 잘못된 시그널을 줄 수 있다는 지적도 나온다.● 野 “北 조선노동당 대변인” 반발 이 대통령의 이 발언은 19일 기자간담회에서 전작권 관련 질의를 받고 “우리 스스로 방위를 감당할 수 있다”는 설명을 하는 과정에서 나왔다. 이 대통령은 핵 전력을 뺀 재래식 군사력이 세계 5위이고, 국방비 지출 수준이 북한의 연간 총생산(GDP) 다 합친 것의 1.5배가량 된...

items.title: 해군 “2040년대 초까지 3만t급 ‘드론 항모’ 확보”
items.snippet: 해군이 2040년 초까지 3만 t급 이상의 ‘유·무인전력모함’을 확보할 계획이라고 20일 밝혔다. 문재인 정부 때부터 경항공모함 도입을 적극 추진했지만, 현대전에서 드론 등 무인전력의 위력이 입증되면서 유·무인전력모함으로 전력 증강 계획을 변경한 것. 해군은 이날 국회 국방위원회 국정감사 업무보고 자료에서 지난해 10월 경항모 건조 사업을 유·무인전력모함으로 소요를 수정 제기했고, 합동참모본부가 현재 검토 중이라고 설명했다. 연내 소요 수정을 최종 결정한 뒤 2040년대 초까지 전력화를 목표로 하고 있다는 것이다. ‘드론항모’로도 불리는 유·무인전력모함에는 해상무인전투기와 감시정찰 및 자폭용 드론 등 무인전력 위주로 탑재된다. 해군이 추진하는 유·무인전력모함은 길이 270m, 폭 70m, 배수량은 3만 t급 이상으로 기존에 도입을 검토한 경항...

items.title: 與 ‘메가특구 주52시간 예외’ 눈치보며 시간끌기… 연내 도입 불투명
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 20일 정부의 3대 메가프로젝트를 뒷받침하기 위한 ‘초광역특구법안’을 발의했다. 메가특구 입주 기업에 ‘고소득·연구직 노동자 주 52시간 제외’(화이트칼라 이그젬션) 관련 노동특례 조항 도입 여부는 결정하지 않은 채 이를 포함하는 안과 포함하지 않은 안을 함께 발의한 후 추가 논의를 거치기로 한 것. 고용노동부도 시한을 정하지 않고 원포인트 사회적 대화를 계속 이어간다는 방침을 밝힌 가운데 정부 여당이 노동특례 도입에 대한 결정을 미루면서 계획했던 연내 처리가 불투명해졌다는 전망이 나온다.● 주 52시간제 예외 적용·미적용 법안 함께 발의민주당 한병도 원내대표는 이날 국회에서 열린 국정감사 대책회의에서 초광역특구법안에 대해 “수도권에 집중된 성장의 기회를 전국으로 넓히고 각 지역이 전략 산업을 중심으로 대한민국의 미래를 이끌도록...

items.title: ‘소방 빨대-쭉쭉’ 논란에, 與 내부 “이대론 수도권 총선 망해”

items.title: “현장 구매 되나요?”… ‘오프라인’ 말고 ‘in person’

items.title: 어린이집 0세반, 반년 기다려도 대기 60번
items.snippet: 서울 영등포구에 사는 32세 서모씨는 지난 5월 첫아이를 출산했다. 맞벌이를 하는 서씨는 내년 3월 복직에 맞춰 아이를 어린이집에 보내기 위해 출산 직후 집 근처 어린이집 ‘0세반’ 두 곳에 대기를 걸었다. 하지만 지금까지 대기 순번이 모두 60번대에 머물고 있다. 서씨는 “0세반에 들어가기 어렵다는 건 알았지만 이 정도일 줄은 몰랐다”며 “지금이라도 입주 도우미를 알아봐야 할지, 복직을 미뤄야 할지 막막하다”고 했다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [알립니다] 에듀조선 NIE 지도사 2급 수강생 모집
items.snippet: 에듀조선 NIE(신문 활용 교육) 지도사 양성 과정은 디지털 시대에 필요한 문해력을 키우는 NIE 전문 강사를 양성하는 강좌입니다. 유형별 신문 기사 분석, 활용 전략, 수업 설계 방식 등에 대해 단기간에 체계적으로 배울 수 있도록 수업이 구성돼 있습니다. 2급 자격증을 취득하면 공공기관, 평생교육기관, 방과후 학교 등에서 강사로 활동할 수 있습니다. 2급 자격증은 1급 자격증 취득을 위한 조건으로, 1급까지 취득 시 조선일보 뉴지엄 프로그램 외부 강사 우선 선발 기회를 제공하는 등 다양한 혜택과 기회가 주어집니다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [노벨 문학상] 10대부터 고대 시에 푹 빠져… 훗날 실험적 작품 기반됐죠
items.snippet: 올해 노벨 문학상의 영예는 캐나다 시인 앤 카슨(76)이 안았어요. 시인·번역가·에세이스트·고전학자인 카슨은 형식과 장르에 얽매이지 않는 작가로 유명해요. 문학상 수여 기관인 스웨덴 아카데미(한림원)는 “고전적 전통과 자유롭고 유희적(놀이를 하듯 즐긴다는 의미)인 대화를 나누며, 현대 문학의 새로운 형식을 개척한 대담하고 창의적인 작품 세계를 기린다”며 선정 이유를 밝혔어요. 그의 작품 세계에 대해선 “문헌학자의 집요한 탐구와 새로운 의미를 창조하려는 시인의 열망이 교차한다”고 평했어요.

items.title: Control of Isolated Four-Quadrant Single-Stage Three-/Single-Phase X-Rectifier for EV On-Board Chargers
items.abstract: The single-stage isolated eXtended-functionality rectifier (X-Rectifier) electric vehicle (EV) on-board charger (OBC) employs 650V GaN monolithic bidirectional power transistors (M-BDS) in the input stage, provides sinusoidal input currents and four-quadrant operation in three-phase and split/single phase grids without power derating, operates from asymmetrical three-phase mains, provides reactive power if needed, and supports extremely asymmetric phase loading in standalone vehicle-to-load (V2L) mode. This paper presents a new improved phase-modular control method for the X-Rectifier that enables tracking of arbitrary and independent phase current references regardless of the instantaneous grid voltage (i.e., enables four-quadrant operation). The method supports grid-tied (i.e., grid-to-vehicle, G2V, or vehicle-to grid, V2G) and grid-forming (i.e., V2L) operation. Further, aiming toward...

items.title: Accelerating real-time hybrid-functional calculations with learned ACE and symmetry-based FFT reuse
items.abstract: Real-time hybrid-functional calculations require repeated reconstruction of nonlocal exchange, whose cost grows rapidly with Brillouin-zone sampling. We develop two methods to improve the efficiency of time evolution and spatial processing. The first learns the time evolution of adaptively compressed exchange (ACE) factors and predicts their updates, reducing the frequency of explicit reconstruction. The second uses crystal symmetry to reuse exchange fast Fourier transforms (FFTs) among equivalent real-space points. This symmetry-based FFT reuse (SBFR) reduces the number of FFTs while retaining the full $\bm k$-point sum. The methods can be used with a variety of hybrid functionals, and we use HSE06 in this work. items.title: Nanophotonic Extreme Ultraviolet Polarimeter
items.abstract: Nanophotonic engineering has revolutionized how we manipulate the polarization of visible light. Here, we extend such control to extreme ultraviolet radiation, the spectral region of attosecond science and semiconductor lithography, where transmissive optical elements are lacking. We implement channel waveguides that restrict incident 41-nm-wavelength light to a few modes with defined spatial profiles and propagation constants. By designing the propagation-length-dependent interference of two eigenmodes, we achieve polarization-dependent forward scattering, which we exploit to create a transmissive nanophotonic analyzer that resolves the polarization axis and spectrum of extreme ultraviolet light from a single measurement. With a 0.9°-sensitivity for polarization rotations in a 1-second measurement and single-shot capability, the device opens new experimental opportunities in ultrafast m...

items.title: Charge-conserving creation and annihilation of topological phase singularities in atomically thin semiconductors
items.abstract: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides provide a promising material platform for optical phase manipulation, as rapid variations in their dielectric functions can give rise to topological phase singularities (PSs). However, PS evolution while preserving topological charge conservation has not yet been investigated in exciton enabled PS systems. Here, using atomically thin MoS2 films on sapphire as a model system, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate that the evolution of dielectric dispersion determines the creation, trajectory, merging, and annihilation of optical PSs under topological charge conservation. By varying the MoS2 film thickness, we experimentally realize this evolution through the gradual shrinking of the high energy n-k dispersion loop, which modifies its intersection with the zero reflection condition. items.title: Nanocrystalline cubic boron arsenide growth on GaAs(100) by gas source molecular beam epitaxy
items.abstract: Cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs) is a promising ultrahigh thermal conductivity semiconductor, but its direct synthesis on lattice-mismatched substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the synthesis of nanocrystalline c-BAs thin films on GaAs(100) substrates using gas source molecular beam epitaxy. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals an optimal growth temperature window of 250-400 C to maintain near stoichiometry and suppress severe arsenic loss. Surface and structural characterizations via atomic force microscopy, reflection high-energy electron diffraction, and grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction demonstrate a Volmer-Weber 3D island growth mode and a preferential crystallographic alignment with the GaAs substrate. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy confirms a chemically sharp interface without gallium interdiffusion into the c-BAs layer. These findings establish...

items.title: Multiplexed Label-Free Cytokine Sensing Using a 128x128 CMOS ISFET Array with Flexdym Microfluidic Partitioning
items.abstract: Cytokine-mediated inflammation disorders such as sepsis and cytokine release syndrome demand bedside multiplex panels that resolve pro- and anti-inflammatory dynamics in minutes, yet label-free FET cytokine sensors remain limited to few devices, single analytes, and PDMS packaging that sorbs small molecules and leaches oligomers. We present a CMOS platform pairing a 128 x 128 ion-sensitive field-effect transistor (ISFET) array (SkyWater 130 nm, SiN gate) with a FlexDym 4 x 1 micro-well overlay that partitions the membrane into four chemically independent regions (approximately 2,176 pixels each, square-root-of-N averaging). Two wells carry capture antibodies (anti-IL-6, anti-IL-10), one is a non-specific reference, and one tests specificity; the transduced signal is defined as the differential current relative to the reference signal (Delta I_D(W_n) - Delta I_D(W_3)). items.snippet: 영화에 나오는 유령처럼 어떤 물질이라도 그냥 통과하는 존재가 있습니다. 바로 우주 만물을 이루는 기본 입자 중 하나인 중성미자입니다. 다른 물질과 거의 반응하지 않고 지나가 ‘우주의 유령’이라고 부릅니다. 올해 노벨 물리학상은 남극 얼음 속 천문대인 아이스큐브(IceCube)에서 우주의 유령을 추적해 온 프랜시스 할젠(82) 미국 위스콘신대 매디슨 교수에게 돌아갔습니다. 중성미자는 우주가 탄생한 빅뱅 직후에도 나왔고, 태양의 핵융합이나 원전(原電)의 핵분열 반응에서도 나옵니다. 질량이 거의 없고 전하(정전기의 양)도 띠지 않아 다른 물질과 반응을 하지 않지만, 우주에서 빛의 최소 단위인 광자 다음으로 흔한 입자입니다. 지금 이 순간에도 태양에서 날아온 중성미자 650억개가 새끼손톱 하나 크기의 면적(약 1㎠)을 매초 지나가고 있습니다.

items.abstract: Utility-scale quantum technologies will not only require a well-performing quantum platform, but also classical control hardware that is scalable, efficient, and meets the design requirements set by the quantum system of interest. One approach is the application of silicon CMOS technology, a highly scalable and mature technology, to design application-specific integrated circuits (ASIC) that are optimized for the quantum system. In this work, we present two-qubit control of electron and nuclear spins in NV centres in diamond, using a cryogenic CMOS qubit controller integrated with a diamond quantum device in a cryostat. Using Gate Set Tomography (GST) we characterize the performance of the single-qubit gates on both electron- and carbon nuclear spins, and analyze the limiting noise processes. items.title: Linear Polarimetry of the Solar Corona during the Total Solar Eclipse of 8 April 2024: Multi-Band Observations and HDR Imaging
items.abstract: High-Dynamic-Range (HDR) multi-band linear polarimetry of the solar corona during total solar eclipses provides a vital ground-based diagnostic tool for mapping plasma morphology and magnetic topology in the inner and middle corona. Extracting reliable polarimetric signals requires rigorous observational calibration, spatial co-alignment, and noise reduction via stacking. We report optical linear polarimetric observations acquired during the 8 April 2024 total solar eclipse from Dallas, Texas, USA, near solar maximum. Using a full-frame color CMOS detector paired with an 80~mm refractor, multi-band Red, Green, and Blue (RGB) images were recorded simultaneously across three polarizer orientations ($-60^\circ$, $0^\circ$, and $+60^\circ$) using a 9-step exposure bracket ($1/800\text{~s}$ to $1/3\text{~s}$). items.title: Privacy-Preserving Robust Monitoring of Dense-Time Temporal Logic
items.abstract: Motivated by the use of third-party testing, this paper presents a privacy-preserving implementation of the robustness monitoring of Signal Temporal Logic (STL). STL is a specification language for systems whose output traces have real-valued timestamps -- most prominently, cyber-physical systems. Its robust semantics, which assign real rather than binary truth values, are an essential ingredient of systems testing and runtime monitoring. In a number of system testing scenarios, the designer and the tester are separate parties. This testing-as-a-service model is common in software, avionics, and semiconductors, and is growing in importance in the red-teaming of machine learning models. In such a model, the designer seeks to preserve the privacy (or secrecy) of its design, while the tester seeks to preserve the privacy of its collateral, including the detailed specification suite. items.title: Anchored Exploration in Product Evolution: A Phylogenetic Network Framework for Semiconductor Designs
items.abstract: We develop a product phylogenetic network framework for examining anchored exploration. Using 102,465 semiconductor products grouped into 45,996 design families, we distinguish accumulated design continuity (Anchor) from externally precedented feature additions (horizontal transfer, HT). Fitted regressions yield non-monotonic relationships for HT occurrence and descendant carriage, alongside increasing within-family carriage over observed support. These patterns connect technological trajectories and recombination by distinguishing the continuity associated with incorporating external features from that associated with reproducing them in subsequent products.

items.title: Superradiant temporal transition radiation of a relativistic electron beam
items.abstract: A charge in uniform motion carries a bound field that does not radiate. Transition radiation releases part of it at a boundary in space. We propose and analyze the case of radiation emission due to a boundary in time: a relativistic electron bunch passes through an aperture in a semiconductor (silicon) wafer, and while its bound field occupies the wafer, a femtosecond laser switches the semiconductor into an electron-hole plasma. The field is a valid solution of the old medium and not of the new one, so it is handed to the plasma as an initial condition for radiation emission at the plasma frequency. Because in temporal transition radiation (t-TR) the wavevector is conserved, and the frequency is not, the emission can appear in a spectral band that the bunch's own field does not populate. items.title: Molecular Doping of MoS$_2$ with N-Heterocyclic Carbenes: A Raman Study of Interfacial Charge Transfer
items.abstract: We demonstrate efficient electron doping of exfoliated MoS$_2$ through the deposition of N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) molecules onto its surface. Raman spectroscopy reveals a pronounced softening of the optical A$_{1g}$ phonon mode after NHC deposition, consistent with electron transfer from the NHC molecules to the MoS$_2$ layers. The largest phonon-energy shifts are observed in monolayer and bilayer flakes whereas changes in bulk-like MoS$_2$ are negligible, indicating that the doping efficiency depends on the number of layers. This thickness dependence highlights the dominant role of interfacial charge transfer at the NHC/MoS$_2$ interface. Quantitative analysis of the Raman modes of as-exfoliated and NHC-covered MoS$_2$, together with comparison with literature values, allows us to estimate an increase in the two-dimensional electron density of about two-orders of magnitude in MoS$_2...

items.title: Epitaxial Displacement-etched GaAsSb Quantum Dots Emitting at Telecom Wavelengths
items.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are essential components for integrated photonic and quantum information systems, yet current epitaxial growth techniques face significant limitations in complexity of growth, material selection, and density tunability. Here we report a displacement etch technique that enables controlled formation of GaAsSb QDs with emission at telecommunications wavelengths. Our approach uses arsenic molecular flux (As$_2$) to react with antimonide surfaces through thermodynamically favorable displacement reactions, creating three-dimensional quantum confined nanostructures without requiring strain-driven growth or complex droplet-based processes. By contrast, the gate fidelity is impacted by differential detuning errors. items.title: Water-Driven Porous Silicon as a Platform for Blue Materials
items.abstract: Living organisms control water to transport matter, transfer energy and drive chemical reactions. In this perspective, we argue that porous silicon can give engineering materials comparable control over water. Its pore architecture, surface chemistry and semiconducting skeleton can be shaped across length scales with the precision of semiconductor processing and, like the water it can host, it relies on one of the most abundant chemical elements on Earth. Liquids in porous silicon, most often water, can flow as a continuum through pores a few nanometers wide, strain the skeleton through capillary and electrosorption stresses, shift structural color, switch transparency, and modulate or generate electrical signals. items.title: Gate-defined quantum dot and charge noise analysis in a Forksheet transistor
items.abstract: We report the cryogenic characterization of a 14-nm nMOS Forksheet transistor down to 10 mK. We demonstrate that the device retains transistor operation with improved characteristics at cryogenic temperatures, while also forming a gate-defined quantum dot that can be tuned to the single-electron regime. In the quantum-dot regime, we perform low-frequency charge-noise measurements across different charge occupations and observe an average charge-noise amplitude of $\langle S_0\rangle = 10\;μ\mathrm{eV}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ at 1 Hz, with a minimum measured value of $3.3\;μ\mathrm{eV}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$. These results highlight the potential of Forksheet technology for the monolithic cointegration of quantum and classical CMOS functionalities in future quantum processors.

items.title: Revealing Detailed Transport Mechanisms in Silicon Tunneling Diodes
items.abstract: Understanding carrier transport in heavily doped semiconductor junctions is essential for developing next-generation tunneling devices for cryogenic electronics and steep-slope technologies. In this work, we investigate the transport mechanisms in a silicon tunneling diode using extensive TCAD (Technology Computer Aided Design) simulations benchmarked against electrical measurements over a wide temperature range of 4 K to 440 K. The measured device characteristics show no negative differential conductance, strong temperature dependence of forward current with a nearly constant semi-logarithmic slope, and weak temperature dependence under high reverse bias. To identify the mechanisms underlying these characteristics, we investigate the contributions of band-to-band tunneling (BTBT), trap-assisted tunneling (TAT), Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) recombination, and avalanche generation. items.title: Engineering nonrelativistic spin splitting in semiconductors by altermagnetic proximity
items.abstract: Altermagnets combine vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting, offering functionalities attractive for spintronics and quantum devices. Their practical use, however, is constrained by the limited availability of materials that simultaneously possess the required altermagnetic symmetry, semiconducting electronic structure, and weak spin-orbit coupling. Here we show that these requirements can instead be separated between constituent materials through proximity engineering. We develop an analytical theory for a conventional semiconductor coupled to a gapped $d$-wave altermagnet and demonstrate that virtual tunneling transfers the altermagnetic spin splitting to the semiconductor. items.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
items.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $μ$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

items.title: Robust Data-Driven Controller Synthesis from Sampled and Uncertain Frequency Response Estimates using Integral Quadratic Constraints
items.abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel MIMO controller synthesis method that relies solely on frequency-domain data of discrete-time systems. The approach is based on an iterative design procedure using \emph{integral quadratic constraints} (IQCs). It generalizes existing data-driven methods that approximate semi-infinite IQC conditions by enforcing them on a finite set of measured frequency points. Such approximations do not provide guarantees on the continuous frequency axis and may fail to capture inter-frequency behavior. We address this limitation by formulating a convex optimization problem that preserves robustness guarantees over the entire frequency range. In particular, the proposed method explicitly accounts for inter-frequency behavior of both plant and controller, leading to certified robust stability and performance. items.title: The Reciprocal tau-Cell: A Log-Domain Circuit for On-Chip Learning
items.abstract: Training hardware by gradient descent requires a gradient to be computed using a separate backwards pass. If a circuit is reciprocal, meaning every connection is symmetric, the backward pass is the same network run a second time with the error as its input. The reciprocal tau-cell, a weak-inversion log-domain circuit, makes this practical in standard CMOS. Each cell is a current-mode leaky integrator with a built-in ReLU; each connection is two transistors whose signed strength is a ratio of bias currents. The equilibrium of the network is the solution to a convex program, and latching the cells that are off will hardware linearise the circuit, making its second run exactly linear. items.title: On-sky performance and prospects of near-infrared CMOS detectors in exoplanet detection: first year of SPIRIT
items.abstract: Ultracool dwarfs are promising targets for detecting and characterising temperate terrestrial exoplanets. Their flux peaks in the near-infrared, beyond the wavelength cut-off of the silicon-based CCDs used by ground-based surveys dedicated to observing them, such as SPECULOOS. We present the on-sky performance of SPIRIT (SPeculoos InfraRed Imager for Transits), an InGaAs CMOS detector on the Callisto telescope at the SPECULOOS Southern Observatory, during its first year of operation, from mid-2022 to 2023. We use 328 visits of 73 targets to optimise our CMOS-specific reduction process, including our approach to glow effects and bad-pixel handling. We find the measured precision to be consistent with our theoretical noise model, achieving sub-part-per-thousand precision under good observing conditions across targets spanning $J$-band magnitudes of 10--13. items.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET)-based compute-in-memory (CIM) promises energy-efficient deep neural network (DNN) inference, but device variation can severely degrade bit-sliced CIM accuracy. Prior works either rely on hardware modifications or treat such variation as generic noise, overlooking a key FeFET asymmetry: negligible off-state leakage makes errors dominated by conducting on-state cells. This asymmetry is amplified by two's-complement sign extension, which maps small negative values to high-significance bit slices and magnifies their errors during shift-and-add reconstruction. In this paper, we propose CAFE, a conducting-cell-aware adaptive differential encoding framework built upon this FeFET-specific asymmetry. items.abstract: Semiconductor moiré superlattices, owing to strongly bound excitons and pronounced electronic correlation, have emerged as an intriguing solid platform for exploring correlated bosonic phenomena, where the moiré potential landscape plays a central role. Hydrostatic pressure allows continuous, in-situ tuning of this landscape, but remains underexplored because of experimental challenges. Here we integrate a diamond anvil pressure cell with high quality dual gated WSe2/WS2 twisted bilayers and perform cryogenic optical spectroscopy. We observe distinct pressure evolutions of moiré intralayer excitons, which reveal drastic modulation of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape captured by a continuum model and suggest the capability of engineering the exciton-band topology. items.abstract: Tracing my scientific path from many-body physics in semiconductor nanostructures to topological quantum matter, this Habilitation à diriger des recherches (HDR) memoir presents only part of my research since defending two PhD theses in Toulouse and Nizhny Novgorod in 2011. Focusing on pseudo-relativistic fermions and topological states in zinc-blende semiconductors and their heterostructures, it highlights my independent research program: identifying physical problems, developing predictive theories, and initiating new directions with experimentalists. The first part addresses Kane fermions in bulk HgCdTe: temperature-driven band inversion, domain-wall states, the collapse of Landau levels in crossed electric and magnetic fields, and disorder-induced topological transitions. items.abstract: Strong coupling between mobile charge carriers or excitons and lattice vibrations gives rise to polarons: quasiparticles formed by charge carriers dressed by a cloud of phonon excitations. Polaron formation determines transport properties of systems ranging from transition-metal oxides and organic semiconductors to light-harvesting complexes. In excitonic systems that admit a hard-core boson description, mapping the excitations to pseudospins provides a natural framework for studying polaron physics, including the nonperturbative regime in which hopping amplitudes, phonon energies, and coupling strengths are comparable. Here, we propose a trapped-ion blueprint for realizing spin-phonon Hamiltonians with programmable spatial coupling between excitation density and phonon displacements, encompassing local Holstein and long-range Fröhlich-type interactions. items.title: Single anyons and anyon binding in a quantum Hall dot
items.abstract: Anyons are particles with quantized fractional statistics. In theory, a single anyon can be stabilized as a localized fractional charge within the bulk of a topologically ordered two-dimensional insulator. However, experiments to date have focused on probing anyons in structures in which many anyonic excitations coexist and interact. Here, we demonstrate the trapping of a single anyon in a device consisting of a graphene-based quantum point contact with an embedded tunable quantum Hall dot. Benchmarking our device at v = 1, we demonstrate backscattering between Fermi liquid edge states mediated by the whole-electron Coulomb blockade of the dot. The cleanliness and control available in our device allow depletion of the dot to the last quasihole, and we observe spin blockade for transitions to the opposite-spin Landau level. items.abstract: Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. items.abstract: The exploration of next-generation wide-gap semiconductors with extreme work functions is highly desirable for the continued advancement of electronic and optoelectronic devices. By using first principles calculations, we show that \b{eta}-TeO3, with a wide band gap exceeding 3 eV, emerges as a promising n-type semiconductor exhibiting ultrahigh work functions of up to ~8 eV. The work function is evaluated across a series of low-index nonpolar surfaces. items.abstract: While most studies on Co$2$MnAl (CMA) focus on the ultrathin regime for spintronic junctions, applications scaling with magnetic volume--such as Anomalous Nernst Effect (ANE) energy harvesters, integrated power inductors, and magnetic MEMS--require significantly thicker films. In contrast, samples on Si substrates exhibit a disorder transition toward the A2 phase, closely linked to diffusion-driven degradation processes. items.title: ARES: a plane-wave density-functional-theory code in Rust
items.abstract: ARES (Ab initio atomic mateRial modEling Software at JLU) is a plane-wave density-functional-theory (DFT) code written entirely in Rust as a layered 22-crate workspace. It supports norm-conserving pseudopotentials and the projector augmented-wave (PAW) method with the local-density approximation (LDA) and Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) functionals, Γ-only and explicit k-point sampling, smearing and mixing, forces, stress, relaxation, band structures, densities of states (DOS) and dispersion corrections; execution is serial or MPI-distributed over k-point pools, band groups and plane-wave rows. The code's distinguishing engineering choice is its validation apparatus. items.title: Theory of deeply subwavelength electromagnetic structuring of semiconductors due to thermal-ionization instability
items.abstract: We develop a theory of ionization-assisted instability that governs the reflection of intense electromagnetic pulses from a semiconductor surface. Local overheating of the material increases the free-carrier density and conductivity, which in turn enhances the absorption of the incident radiation and further amplifies local heating and avalanche ionization. At high pump repetition rates, the overheating accumulates from pulse to pulse, leading to a gradual rise of the local material temperature and free carrier density - a positive feedback loop that drives thermal runaway. However, this effect competes with diffraction of the pump field on the emerging perturbation of the dielectric permittivity or on the surface relief, which reduces the local electric field amplitude in the overheated regions, thus providing negative feedback. items.abstract: We present first-principles calculations of the electron-hole-pair creation energy in semiconductors and dielectrics, focusing in particular on AlN, 3C-SiC, 4H-SiC, Si, and SiO2. We have employed density functional theory (DFT) to calculate the band structure, density-functional perturbation theory to obtain the phonon dispersion, and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) to calculate the electron energy loss function (via the dielectric function). We performed full-band Monte Carlo simulations of electron thermalization for energies up to ~100 eV and calculated the average energy required to excite an electron-hole pair. We calculated pair-creation energies of approximately 12.2, 6.5, 7.3, 3.10, and 16.7 eV/pair for AlN, 3C-SiC, 4H-SiC, Si, and SiO2, respectively. items.abstract: We propose a novel amorphous oxide semiconductor (AOS)-based conductive-semiconducting-conductive (CSC) MOS test structure to effectively sense, discriminate, and analyze distinct trap-induced conductance losses in AOS transistors. The CSC architecture mitigates these contact-related artifacts, enabling the decoupling of interface states and shallow states. Furthermore, the contributions from leakage, series resistance, and device-geometry effects are identified and calibrated. Our results yield bias-resolved trap profiles and reveal three distinct regimes: (1) In the depletion region, interface states dominate the conductance loss. items.abstract: Four-level indium-gallium-zinc oxide (IGZO) 2T0C memory needs reliable state formation, sensing references, and a path from cell errors to digital weights. items.abstract: In this study, an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation of the refractive indices of different materials is performed. The evaluation of the refractive index is necessary to design photonic devices for various classical and quantum photonic applications, and to theoretically analyse experimental results. The refractive index is one of the crucial parameters that affect the interaction of light with matter. Although the refractive index can be measured experimentally, its estimation via computational means provide the advantage of not requiring costly instrumentation, trained researchers and could avoid potential laboratory-based uncertainties. Therefore, in this study, artificial intelligence is implemented to estimate the optical constants of two types of materials, i.e., noble metals, and semiconductors. items.title: Stateless Stochastic Computing for Generative AI on Superconducting Logic: A Model-Hardware Co-Design
items.abstract: Thermodynamic computing lets stochastic physical dynamics carry out a computation and reads out the result as a time average. Recently, thermodynamic computing has been demonstrated on several hardware platforms, including digital CMOS circuits based on stochastic computing. Superconducting single-flux-quantum (SFQ) logic offers very high clock rates and very low switching energy, but it heavily penalizes state, memory, fan-out, and feedback, i.e., exactly the per-neuron accumulators on which such designs rely. We therefore realize thermodynamic computing in SFQ logic through a co-design of a generative model and its circuit in which the datapath holds no state at all. items.title: Localized Joule heating and carbonization process optimization of 3D printed polymer structures for lab-on-CMOS applications
items.abstract: Use of carbon electrodes integrated with CMOS technology has great promise for lab-on-chip, biomedical, environmental, and industrial applications. One method of developing carbon electrodes is to 3D print polymer nanostructures on a CMOS chip, and use a thermal annealing process to pyrolyze them into carbon at high temperature, approximately 950 °C. items.title: TileCas: Cascading Kernel Development Across Programming Abstractions
items.abstract: Programming abstractions have traditionally been designed for humans, but code generation is increasingly performed by models and autonomous agents. We investigate abstractions for machine-driven programming through GPU and AI-accelerator kernel generation. High-level domain-specific languages (DSLs) simplify search by delegating implementation details to compilers, while lower-level representations provide finer-grained control at the cost of a larger and more complex search space. In this paper, we present TileCas, a unified, pluggable interface that enables coding agents to develop kernels across multiple editable abstraction levels. items.abstract: A Muon Collider is one of the most attractive routes to multi-TeV lepton collisions, but it requires the accelerator and detector communities to solve a tightly coupled set of problems that have no close precedent in an operating collider. Muons must be produced, captured, cooled, accelerated, and collided before they decay. The detector must then extract clean physics from an environment dominated by decay products from the beamline. Artificial intelligence is not a substitute for accelerator physics, detector design, or engineering validation. It is, however, unusually well matched to several of the central obstacles: high-dimensional design spaces, expensive simulations, coupled subsystem trade-offs, and workflows that are currently too slow or too fragile to support broad design exploration. items.title: Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
items.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. items.title: DFIT: A Framework for Building Instrumentation Tools Across Heterogeneous Dataflow Accelerators
items.abstract: Emerging dataflow accelerators offer exceptional energy efficiency and throughput for machine learning workloads, yet remain largely opaque to developers for performance analysis. Unlike CPUs and GPUs, where instrumentation frameworks enable fine-grained introspection, dataflow hardware exposes little information. This lack of transparency limits the ability of compiler engineers, system designers, and application developers to analyze, tune, or debug accelerator behavior. In this paper, we introduce DFIT (DataFlow Accelerator Instrumentation Tool), an instrumentation framework designed specifically for dataflow architectures. DFIT directly instruments operations, regions, and compiler transformations at the graph IR and backend-lowering stages using semantic program representation. DFIT captures high-level, semantically meaningful data that reflect the true dataflow of computation. Thes...

items.title: Predicting Nanofabrication Variance: A Conditional Diffusion Model
items.abstract: Micro- and nanostructures fabricated by focused ion beam (FIB) milling invariably deviate from input designs due to systematic and stochastic effects such as ablation-rate fluctuations, and redeposition. As such, nominally identical iterations of a given process yield a distribution of non-identical fabrication outcomes, leading to variations in the physical (optical, mechanical) properties of fabricated structures. Existing models of the milling process typically predict a single deterministic fabrication result, neglecting this variability. Here we present a conditional diffusion model that learns the statistical distribution of process outcomes conditioned on input design, enabling it to predict a realistic distribution of possible output sample structures. These predictions accurately reproduce edge morphology, linewidth variations, and defect probabilities observed in fabricated sam...

items.title: Bottom-Up Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering for the Detection of Micro-Objects and Globular Analytes
items.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is typically achieved by depositing the analyte on a metal or semiconductor substrate. We propose a bottom-up approach, enabling SERS by depositing a metal on the surface of the object being studied. A Mie-theory analysis of electric-field enhancement in dielectric core-shell particles is presented. A correlative approach combining SERS, atomic force microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy is employed to model the conditions required for sensitive SERS detection and spectral analysis of polystyrene microspheres (PMSs) as models of globular and vesicle-like objects. Based on these findings, we propose a SERS-active system that provides strong signal enhancement (up to four orders of magnitude for a single globular object) while maintaining spectral fidelity, where PMSs act both as model analytes and as integral components of a metal-dielectric...

items.title: Theory of exciton-exciton interactions with nontrivial electronic bands
items.abstract: Excitons are bound electron-hole pairs in semiconductors whose interactions influence optical properties and determine their collective behavior and emergent correlated phases. Despite the theoretical and experimental significance of these phenomena, a microscopic theory of exciton-exciton interactions that takes into account the full composite nature of these quasiparticles in systems with an arbitrary single-particle Hamiltonian is lacking. Here, we present a general theory of exciton-exciton interactions that builds upon our previous publication [Physical Review B 113, 155440 (2026)], which applied only to conventional semiconductors with weak band hybridization. By contrast, the theory presented here is valid in virtually any crystalline semiconducting system and can be applied to the study of biexciton formation and correlated excitonic phases in systems where band topology, quantum...

items.title: Orbital transfer reveals material-selective structure in Rydberg excitons
items.abstract: Rydberg excitons in atomically thin semiconductors offer a sensitive view of dielectric screening and electronic structure. As their spectra become increasingly well resolved, a central question is how much material information an effective Hamiltonian can predict beyond the states used to determine it. Using the 1s, 2p and 2s levels to determine a scalar Rytova-Keldysh Hamiltonian, we test its transfer to the excluded 3p state. The transfer deviations have opposite signs: the observed 3p lies 7.38 meV below the prediction in MoSe2 and 5.58 meV above it in WS2; the opposite signs persist across the complete reported +/-2-sigma peak-error boxes. In a separate high-field-calibrated benchmark, RK removes 66.8% of the orbital error of a pure two-dimensional Coulomb reference, making the remaining state-selective deviations particularly informative. items.title: Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium
items.abstract: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. By moving the Fermi level towards the Weyl point, we observe a pronounced enhancement of negative magnetoresistance, which arises from chiral anomaly and robustly persists up to ambient temperature. Beyond the quantum limit, the system exhibits positive linear magnetoconductance, serving as a compelling transport signature of the chiral anomaly in the lowest Landau level. Notably, in the extreme quantum limit at cryogenic temperatures, the magnetoresistance undergoes a dramatic reversal from negative to positive. This reversal points to a potential...

items.title: From Prompts to Silicon: Scaling LLM-Assisted Chip Design with the AI Hardware Design League
items.abstract: The semiconductor workforce shortage has renewed interest in making chip design accessible to students without conventional very-large-scale integration (VLSI) training. We present the AI Hardware Design League (AI-HDL), an international, project-based competition in which students use Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate and iteratively refine Verilog while simulation, synthesis, timing analysis, security review, and physical verification provide the engineering feedback needed to validate the result. Across two annual cycles, AI-HDL grew from 172 to 604 participants and from 40 to 108 teams, reaching 30 universities, six community colleges, and 19 countries. In the 2026 cohort, 68.7% of participants reported no prior Verilog experience. Twenty-two teams completed the four design phases and reached final evaluation. items.title: Nonlocal Josephson coupling and current redistribution in a large-area graphene multiterminal Josephson junction
items.abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) extend conventional two-terminal Josephson physics to devices defined by multiple superconducting phases, where rich phenomena have been predicted. However, in conventional MTJJs, superconducting transport is often dominated by local coupling between neighboring leads, obscuring physics that goes beyond simple connectivity. Here, we realize a multiterminal Josephson network in a graphene Hall bar geometry with micron-scale dimensions, enabling substantial nonlocal coupling between distant terminals. Our key observation is a pronounced negative differential longitudinal resistance (NDLR) in the four-probe response near switching currents, while no such feature appears in two-terminal measurements. items.abstract: Students often perceive scientific experiments as clean, straightforward procedures with predictable outcomes. Students' beliefs about the nature of experimental physics typically remain inconsistent through the initial stages of undergraduate education. In reality, experimental work in physics involves hands-on activities such as soldering circuits, assembling provisional setups, and building functional mock-ups from simple materials before reliable measurements can be achieved. To address this gap, we designed a laboratory activity in which students were completely involved in the experiment design, construction and operation with the final goal of measuring the speed of light with a low-cost and compact setup. items.title: An all-transistor physical-learning transformer can be trained to perform in-context learning
items.abstract: Most systems trained by equilibrium propagation or coupled learning are in the same class as multi-layer perceptrons: while they may be universal function approximators, they struggle to learn associative tasks which are easy for transformers. Equilibrium propagation relies on a bidirectional flow of information through the physical system between input and output. The reverse flow is broken by more complex nonlinear systems, such as those performing multiplication which is needed to express dot-product attention. Here we explicitly restore this bidirectional flow by introducing extra circuit elements for this purpose into a double or dyadic circuit. We then use these ideas to construct an attention mechanism exploiting the exponential current law of sub-threshold MOSFET devices. We show that in simulations this circuit can be trained to perform a simple in-context learning task, despite...

items.title: Spatiotemporal computing for temporal nonlinear tasks using few-mode fiber and SOA nonlinearity
items.abstract: Step-index few-mode fibers (FMFs) provide a compact passive platform for high-speed photonic information processing by exploiting modal dispersion to map temporal inputs into spatiotemporal representations with short-term memory. In previous studies, we have demonstrated linear classification tasks with such FMFs, such as ultrafast multibit header recognition. Here, we extend the computational capability of such architectures towards solving nonlinear tasks by introducing an optical nonlinearity at the output of the dispersive medium. The FMF output is processed through parallel direct and nonlinear branches, with the latter implemented using a nonlinear semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA). We experimentally evaluate the architecture at 28.5 Gb/s on two delayed XOR and higher-order parity tasks. Across five diagnostic datasets (bearing vibration, process monitoring, semiconductor equipment), we study whether an LLM can reliably use external diagnostic information; paired repeat calls separate advice effects from output instability. In all five, conflicting external information overturned initially correct LLM judgments. Among the four datasets with direct integration comparisons, none showed a consistent advantage for implicit LLM integration over the stronger standalone source. On a Tennessee Eastman confirmation set whose protocol was fixed before evaluation, unaided accuracy was 64.67%, implicit LLM-specialist integration 77.43%, and the specialist alone 83.33%. items.abstract: Spin qubits are an attractive platform for scalable quantum computation, and recently, laterally gated quantum dots (QDs) in Ge heterostructures have emerged as a leading implementation. We resolve QD loading and interdot transitions with both techniques. items.title: Hall conductance of dilute electrolytes from odd stochastic density functional theory
items.abstract: Electrolytes under an external magnetic field exhibit a Hall conductivity, much like metals and semiconductors. However, existing theories fail to quantitatively account for their measured Hall conductivities. To make progress toward such a theory, we develop a stochastic density functional framework for electrolytes in a magnetic field. This framework, which we dub odd SDFT, extends the celebrated stochastic density functional theory (SDFT) to incorporate transverse mobilities and chiral time-correlated noise. Using this framework, we calculate the Hall conductivity in the absence of hydrodynamic solvent effects through three approaches: (i) direct response, (ii) Green-Kubo relation, and (iii) a hybrid fluctuation-dissipation relation. We further show that odd SDFT applies more broadly to fluids with broken time-reversal and mirror symmetry, including odd-diffusive fluids and chiral act...

items.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
items.abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for NV- decoherence in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters invert that attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.1-7.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies, over three decades of concentration. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts...

items.title: Device contacts as spin-state selectors for silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
items.abstract: Optically addressable defect spins in semiconductors are promising building blocks for scalable quantum technologies. Yet, the consequences of conventional contact schemes used in semiconductor device integration for the quantum spin environment remain largely unexplored. Using the silicon vacancy (V$_\mathrm{Si}$) in silicon carbide (SiC) as a model system, we show that a widely used contact metal, nickel (Ni), intrinsically perturbs the defect spin state and quenches the characteristic emission from the spin-quartet channel of V$_\mathrm{Si}$. Low-energy muon spin rotation further reveals that Ni contacts create a magnetically contaminated region extending at least $\sim$110 nm into the SiC, in stark contrast to non-magnetic contacts such as Ti and Al. Moreover, cross-sectional cathodoluminescence measurements on samples with high defect density demonstrate a suppressed quartet-state l...

items.title: A semiconductor photon-pair source based on a polariton cascade
items.abstract: We present a theoretical study of a semiconductor photon-pair source based on a radiative cascade enabled by a permanent exciton dipole. The source consists of a GaAs quantum dot placed between a metal nanoparticle and a mirror. The dot exciton and the localized electromagnetic mode mix to form upper and lower polaritons. Without a permanent dipole, a symmetry separating states with even and odd excitation numbers forbids photon emission between the polaritons. Separation of the mean electron and hole positions gives the exciton a permanent dipole and breaks this symmetry. The upper polariton can then emit an idler photon as it decays to the lower polariton. The lower polariton can emit a signal photon as the system returns to its ground state. Using an effective model, we calculate the probability that a prepared upper polariton emits both photons through the metal antenna. We also anal...

items.title: An Emerging NVM-Based On-Chip Training Architecture with Non-Ideality Mitigation Through Bipolar Weight Distributions
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning has presented significant energy efficiency challenges to the conventional von Neumann architecture. In-memory computing (IMC) architectures based on emerging non-volatile memory (eNVM) are widely regarded as a promising solution for accelerating neural network training due to their high parallelism and low power consumption. However, the intrinsic non-idealities of eNVM devices can cause conductance updates to deviate from target values, thereby limiting the performance of on-chip training. To address this challenge, this paper presents a Non-ideality Optimized eNVM Accelerator (NOVA) architecture for on-chip training. Specifically, we first fabricate a two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) and develop a conductance modulation behavioral model calibrated with experimental data. Building upon this device model, we propos...

items.title: Optically Coupled Noise Spectroscopy Quantifies Defect Passivation in Monolayer MoS2 FETs
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers are promising materials for electronic and photonic applications, yet the performance of chemical vapour deposition grown samples is severely limited by native sulphur vacancies that introduce mid-gap trap states, degrade carrier mobility, and elevate electrical noise. Here we investigate octanethiol passivation of sulphur vacancies in monolayer MoS2 field effect transistors, combining x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, photoluminescence, and Raman scattering with electrical transport and optically coupled low-frequency noise spectroscopy. Thiol treatment reduces the sulphur vacancy concentration from 7% to 4%, reducing the free electron density. Electrically, it increases the device resistance 35-fold while restoring gate switching with an on/off ratio of 10^4 and improving field-effect mobility from 1 to 5 cm^2/Vs. Low frequency noise spectrosc...

items.title: On-chip nanoplasma for adaptive electromagnetic protection
items.abstract: Over the past decade, semiconductor diodes have served as the primary switching elements in adaptive electromagnetic (EM) protection, yet their performance has been compromised by parasitic effects and thermal accumulation, rendering them inadequate against the rapidly evolving landscape of high-power microwave (HPM) threats. Here we show that on-chip nanoplasma switches (NPMS), composed of gallium nitride electrodes on silicon carbide substrates, exhibit superior radio frequency (RF) and thermal characteristics, positioning them as ideal field-driven switches in RF front-end protectors. By integrating NPMS into metasurfaces, antennas and circuit limiters, we achieve an adaptive response that ensures low-loss transmission for normal signals and high shielding against HPMs, while offering extended operating bandwidth and substantially higher tolerance than conventional solid-state devices...

items.title: Odd-even dichotomy in the waveforms of modified Emden oscillators of arbitrary integer power
items.abstract: Closed-form waveforms of the modified Emden oscillators $\ddot x+(q+2)kx^q\dot x+k^2x^{2q+1}+ω^2x=0$ of arbitrary natural power $q$, and of their damped $c$-deformed versions, are obtained through a generalized commutative factorization that reduces them to Bernoulli equations. We show that commutative factorizations of Liénard equations are gauge-conjugated forms of the nonlocal linearizing transformation of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Kundu and Lakshmanan, the factorization constant being half the difference of the roots of the associated linear oscillator. These oscillators display an odd--even dichotomy: for odd $q$ they are isochronous, with period $2π/ω$ independent of the amplitude, within an explicitly bounded range of the integration constant, while for even $q$ the oscillations decay algebraically, as $t^{-1/q}$. The dichotomy is confirmed by an elliptic polar representation, i...

items.title: Approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser for reducing energy consumption
items.abstract: Photonic reservoir computing is a promising physical machine-learning approach for time-series prediction. Quantization of the reservoir response signal is an important consideration in the implementation of photonic reservoir computing, and the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency need to be optimized to achieve high prediction performance and low energy consumption. However, few studies have investigated the effects of the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency on both prediction performance and energy consumption. In this study, we introduce the concept of approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser by quantizing the reservoir node states and output weights. We numerically evaluate the performance of a chaotic time-series prediction task and estimate the energy consumption per sample using a component-level model. By optimizing the number of qu...

items.title: Photon-conserving Raman soliton attractors in focusing and defocusing Kerr media
items.abstract: The sign of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient has long been regarded as irrelevant to the direction of the Raman-induced soliton self-frequency shift. Yet the standard generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) predicts a frequency shift that depends on the sign of the nonlinearity, which leads to an unphysical blue shift in the defocusing case. We resolve this inconsistency by deriving the time-domain form of the photon-conserving GNLSE (pcGNLSE) from its established frequency-domain counterpart. The derivation reveals that photon-number conservation imposes two sign modifications relative to the standard GNLSE: the Raman-shift coefficient acquires the absolute value of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient in place of its signed counterpart, and the self-steepening-Raman dissipation term likewise carries an absolute-value prefactor rather than a signed one. These two modifications jointl...

items.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
items.abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^ζ$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. These states show that the non-Ohmic response emerges from voltage-driven percolation. Conduction is governed by how junctions are conne...

items.title: Complex frequency-dependent quadrature squeezing in semiconductor lasers
items.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of quadrature squeezing in a quantum well laser based on a fully quantum Langevin approach. We compute the frequency-resolved squeezing map of the laser field and identify optimal squeezing curves, revealing, for the first time to our knowledge, both frequency-dependent squeezing and complex or hidden squeezing in a semiconductor laser. We further analyse the role of the linewidth enhancement factor (alpha-factor) in the emergence of these features. Our results establish semiconductor lasers as a platform for the generation of non-classical light and open new perspectives for their application in quantum communication and sensing.

items.title: Electron state tomography from quasiparticle interference maps
items.abstract: Characterizing electronic band structures requires precise knowledge of wave functions and their quantum geometry. Here, we introduce a tomography method to reconstruct the density matrix of electron states from quasiparticle interference maps around single impurities. We consider two-orbital models on a honeycomb lattice, relevant to graphene heterostructures and direct-gap semiconductors. For on-site impurities, backscattering between time-reversed states directly maps the density matrix populations and coherences into distinct orbital contributions in the interference map. While local probes usually lack orbital resolution, these orbital contributions transform under distinct symmetry group representations and can thus be disentangled to reveal the density matrix and quantum geometric tensor of the scattering states. This establishes impurities as tomographic probes for band structure...

items.title: Nanoscopic Multiplexing Optical Data Storage via Chip Fabrication
items.abstract: The accelerating growth of global data demands storage technologies combining high capacity, long lifetime and low energy consumption. Optical storage is attractive for archival applications, but conventional optical writing is constrained by diffraction-limited resolution and scalability, while thermal accumulation limits high-speed writing. Here we shift optical data writing from a serial optical process to a fabrication-defined process, in which lithographic masks govern where material modification occurs. Using patterned resist masks and ion implantation, we create fluorescent information voxels with nanoscale control over millimeter-scale areas. The platform supports multilevel and multidimensional encoding by independently encoding information in fluorescence intensity and wavelength. A machine-learning-assisted super-resolution reconstruction protocol is developed to recover infor...

items.title: Absorption and Phase-Contrast Microtomography Using Direct X-Ray Detection With Commercial Off-The-Shelf CMOS Sensors
items.abstract: This work presents high-resolution X-ray microtomography based on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) CMOS image sensors as direct detectors. The system uses a microfocus X-ray source in cone-beam geometry, enabling both absorption-contrast imaging, thanks to the sensor s intrinsic resolution, and phase-contrast imaging, by adjusting the object-to-sensor distance. A dynamic flat-field correction algorithm mitigates radiation-induced sensor degradation during long acquisitions. The setup provides voxel sizes from 3.9 microns to 5.2 microns, with an effective spatial resolution (FWHM) as fine as 9.6 microns in magnified phase-contrast mode (1.33x) and 21 microns in non-magnified absorption-contrast mode. Phase contrast enhances visualization of soft tissue boundaries that are difficult to visualize using absorption-contrast imaging in the same experimental configuration.

items.title: Exciton-Tunable Phase Control and Superstrong Coupling Through Multimode Polariton Engineering in Planar Waveguides
items.abstract: Strong light-matter coupling in optical waveguides provides a versatile platform for engineering hybrid polaritonic modes and their dispersion. Here we investigate multimode exciton-photon coupling in visible semiconductor waveguides supporting several transverse electric modes. Using rigorous coupled-wave analysis combined with a coupled-oscillator model, we show that the photonic band structure can be engineered across a range of regimes, from conventional multimode strong coupling to the superstrong coupling regime, where the Rabi splitting becomes comparable to the spacing between adjacent photonic modes. In the latter regime, hybridization between orthogonal electromagnetic modes is enabled by restricting the active material to a subregion of the mode volume where the photonic modes exhibit strong mutual overlap. This breaking of the orthogonality leads to polaritonic branches whose...

items.title: Energy Consumption in Next Generation Radio Access Networks
items.abstract: Historically, in macro-cell-based networks, the radio access network (RAN) portion accounts for the largest share of energy consumption in mobile networks. With greater densification, the transition to small cells and increased virtualization of the radio processing functions, the relative energy use of the different network segments is changing. At the same time, open radio access networks (O-RAN) have emerged as a promising approach to support this evolution through open interfaces that enable a multi-vendor environment, support for hierarchical intelligent controls, and simplified, cost-effective radio units that facilitate large-scale deployments. This paper examines the impact of these changes on energy consumption in next-generation RAN architectures through transaction-based energy models.
